daily_brief: Wednesday marks the third anniversary of the October 7, 2023 Hamas-led attacks on Israel, with commemorations across the country even as the conflict's toll continues to mount—over 74,000 Palestinians killed in Gaza according to [Al Jazeera] and [RFI], while [BBC] and [Globe and Mail] report Israelis gathering at massacre sites and the music festival location. In France, a major domestic crisis deepens as the government suspended stun grenade use after a 15-year-old lost his hand during student protests over school conditions; Prime Minister Lecornu will address the nation Wednesday evening [BBC], [France 24], [RFI]. On the health front, Kenya confirmed its first-ever Ebola death from the ongoing DRC outbreak that has killed over 4,000 people [Guardian], while the WHO pressed Russia for transparency on a plague lab worker's death in Siberia—President Trump said he would discuss the matter with Putin [BBC], [The Hindu]. In Stockholm, the Nobel Prize in Chemistry was awarded to France's Henri Kagan and Japan's Kenso Soai for their work on molecular mirror images [Nikkei Asia], [Globe and Mail], [ABC Australia]. Meanwhile, Russia launched one of its largest missile barrages against Ukraine, killing at least 15 civilians on Putin's birthday [BBC].

top_stories.headline: Israel Marks Third Anniversary of October 7 Attacks Amid Ongoing Regional Conflict
bullets: Three years after Hamas-led attacks killed approximately 1,200 Israelis and took 251 hostages, commemorations were held at kibbutzim, bomb shelters, and the Nova music festival site
More than 74,000 Palestinians have been killed in Gaza since Israel's retaliatory campaign began, with over 1,460 killed since the October 2025 ceasefire
All hostages have now returned home, marking the first anniversary without captives still held in Gaza
Israeli troops continue to occupy portions of southern Lebanon in ongoing conflict with Hezbollah, which began supporting Hamas in 2023

top_stories.headline: France Suspends Stun Grenades as Student Protests Escalate; PM to Address Nation
bullets: Interior Minister suspended stun grenade use after a 15-year-old's hand was blown off during Monday protests in Lens
Over 500 schools were fully or partially closed Wednesday, with 24 schools set alight or vandalized affecting 30,000 pupils
An estimated 260,000-450,000 protesters marched Tuesday demanding better school conditions; 488 arrested and 43 security personnel injured
Prime Minister Lecornu scheduled evening address covering school protests, fuel prices, agricultural crisis, and national finances

top_stories.headline: Kenya Reports First-Ever Ebola Death as DRC Outbreak Surpasses 4,000 Fatalities
bullets: A Kenyan man who had lived in DRC for seven years died after traveling through Uganda to Nairobi, marking Kenya's first confirmed Ebola case
The ongoing DRC outbreak of the Bundibugyo strain has killed 4,082 people out of 8,463 confirmed cases since May—the country's 17th outbreak
France announced additional €7 million in funding, bringing its 2026 contribution to €23 million to combat the epidemic
Kenyan authorities identified 28 contacts of the deceased including family members and healthcare workers

top_stories.headline: Trump to Discuss Siberian Plague Lab Death with Putin as WHO Demands Transparency
bullets: A 28-year-old worker at Russia's Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute died last week from suspected pneumonic plague, prompting international concern
WHO Director-General Tedros called for 'timely, complete and transparent information sharing' from Russia under International Health Regulations
President Trump said the US is in 'very deep discussions' and expects to report on his Putin conversation Thursday; Kremlin denies any call is scheduled
Russian officials say contacts of the victim tested negative and have not confirmed pneumonic plague as cause of death

top_stories.headline: Russia Launches Major Missile Barrage Against Ukraine on Putin's Birthday, Killing 15
bullets: At least 15 people killed in overnight strikes across central and eastern Ukraine, including nine in Pryluky where three children's bodies were recovered from rubble
Zelensky described the attack as one of Russia's 'most vile,' noting 70 missiles were fired targeting Kyiv, Dnipro, Kremenchuk, Zaporizhzhia, and other cities
Ukraine conducted retaliatory strikes on Russia's Perm, Samara, and Astrakhan regions and unspecified targets in the Black Sea
Attack coincided with Putin's 74th birthday; Zelensky characterized it as Putin's 'birthday gift' to himself
